newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude slides again with weak US products.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude slides again with weak US products.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures hit the skids on Friday afternoon, under pressure from weak gasoline and heating oil prices in the United States and book squaring ahead of a long weekend, brokers said.
June Brent shed 40 cents to $17.89 a barrel by 1600 GMT, a new low for the session, as NYMEX gasoline and heating oil lost over 1.50 cents a gallon each.
"There's no doubt that U.S. products are leading the way but the thin volumes are not helping Brent. There are just no buyers out there," said a broker.
Brokers pegged June Brent support at $17.81-$17.84 a barrel.
Meanwhile, IPE gas oil also extended earlier losses, sliding $7 to $164.00 a tonne by 1607 GMT, just 75 cents above the session low.

The impact of weak NYMEX heating oil prices was being amplified by slack demand in Europe, where much of the continent is basking in unusually high temperatures, and a narrower arbitrage to the Far East.
Dealers said both contracts were being undermined by long liquidation ahead of a long weekend in Britain.
The IPE will be shut on Monday for a national holiday.
